messages:
Miriam L: Anyone else seeing a tiny duplicated fragment when resuming SSE streams in the browser SDK after token refresh? I have a repro that consistently shows 4-7 chars replayed at the start of the resumed chunk.

Devon R: Is the fragment coming from the end of the last received chunk or a mid-chunk parse? any stack traces or console dumps? :thinking:

Miriam L: It's the tail of the previous chunk. Repro steps:
1) start streaming chat (browser, EventSource polyfill)
2) token TTL expires -> auth refresh triggers reconnect
3) server resumes from seq N
4) UI briefly renders `...wxyz` then the resumed payload starts with `wxyzABCD`

Sam K: That smells like the client parse buffer being preserved across reconnects while the server replays overlapping bytes. Node SDK clears parser state on reconnect; browser polyfill currently keeps it. Parity gap.

Kevin P: Proxy timing matters too. If the reverse proxy closes mid-parse, the polyfill can end up with a dangling partial chunk in its in-memory buffer which then gets prepended to the resumed payload. nginx keepalive/timeout settings reproduce this easily.

Miriam L: here's the simplified parse loop in the polyfill that I think is the culprit:
```
let parseBuf = '';
es.onmessage = (ev) => {
  parseBuf += ev.data;
  const events = parseBuf.split('\n\n');
  parseBuf = events.pop() || '';
  for (const e of events) processEventBlock(e);
}
// reconnect does not clear parseBuf today
```

Devon R: If parseBuf survives reconnect and we also request an inclusive resume from the server, overlap is guaranteed. Two possible fixes: clear parseBuf on reconnect, or change resume semantics so server sends an exclusive offset (i.e., start AFTER last-delivered byte).

Sam K: For SDK parity, we should standardize on exclusive resumption and make both Node and browser accept Last-Event-ID header or a resume_token consistently. Also add a defensive client-side dedupe by sequence number.

Kevin P: Ops action: recommend server-side keepalive colon-heartbeats every ~20s to prevent mid-chunk closures. And document proxy timeouts to avoid drop-in-the-middle behavior. Also ensure keepalives are ignored by the renderer and don’t count for billing.

Miriam L: I'll open a PR that clears parseBuf on reconnect, adds an opt-in `resumeStrategy` option ("exclusive" | "inclusive"; default "exclusive"), and includes a unit test simulating mid-chunk close. Filing issue #4180 with the trace and repro script.

Sam K: Short-term mitigation: browser SDK should fall back to short polling if resume fails more than N times to avoid repeated duplicate tokens in the UI.

ci-bot: started CI for branch fix/sse-polyfill-buffer (build 5177) :rocket:

Devon R: Action items:
- Miriam: PR for buffer clear + resumeStrategy + unit tests
- Sam: spec doc for resume header parity (Last-Event-ID vs resume_token) and client dedupe behavior
- Kevin: infra note for keepalives + recommended proxy settings (nginx example)

Miriam L: thanks — I'll add an e2e that force-closes the TCP conn mid-chunk to validate. Will ping ops for nginx reproducer. Closing here once PR merges. :white_check_mark:
